author: christian-irvine
body:
## Issue
The game needs animations so it looks better.

## Changes
* The player now has animations for the rabbit and rhinos movement
* Added poof effects when you die
* Added poof effects when you jump
* The player now always faces the camera
* The player now flashes when they take damage.

## Things not done and bugs
* There are no animations for the plane
* The player doesn't have a shadow
* When moving and jumping the rabbit slides along the ground in the jump charge animation
* The pin for the respawn is missing so the animation (which temporarily had an aloe vera plant) was never added on spawnpoint update

author: eeshanl
body:
## Description

Add RMR support for IORT and SmmuDxe IoMmu mappings
Parses IORT for RMR node memory range descriptors
Maps them to the SMMU page tables to be used by the IoMmu protocol

Updates TLIBI operation from TLIBI ALL to TLIBI S2 IPA, now invalidates TLB for InputAddress to Stage 2 SMMU.

Due to an issue seen while testing on a physical arm platform, we see a 0x13 F_PERMISSION fault from the smmu when not setting both r/w bits. For now, temporarily setting both RW bits in  IoMmuSetAttribute

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/compare/v13.1.0...v14.0.0)

##### Added

-   support for groups of options and commands in the help using low-level `.helpGroup()` on `Option` and `Command`, and higher-level `.optionsGroup()` and `.commandsGroup()` which can be used in chaining way to specify group title for following options/commands (\[[#​2328](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2328)])

-   remove bogus leading space in help when option has default value but not a description (\[[#​2348](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2348)])
-   `.configureOutput()` now makes copy of settings instead of modifying in-place, fixing side-effects (\[[#​2350](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2350)])

##### Changed

-   *Breaking:* Commander 14 requires Node.js v20 or higher
-   internal refactor of `Help` class adding `.formatItemList()` and `.groupItems()` methods (\[[#​2328](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2328)])

author: cyanchill
body:
# Why

<!--
Please describe the motivation for this PR, and link to relevant GitHub issues, discussions, or feature requests.
-->

This is another attempt at #201, except that we don't upgrade `expo-router` & `react-navigation` since we technically don't need to update them for Expo SDK 52 (and the fact that it does have breaking changes).

At least from early testing, we saw a ~3MB decrease in app size from updating to RN 0.76 (they claim up to a [~3.8MB smaller app bundle](https://reactnative.dev/blog/2024/10/23/release-0.76-new-architecture#android-apps-are-38mb-smaller-thanks-to-native-library-merging)).

Also utilize new `expo-file-system/next` & `expo-image-manipulator` APIs.

body:
This pull request introduces several updates, including the removal of the `CONTRIBUTING.md` file, enhancements to the documentation, and the addition of a new `version` command to the Rocketship CLI. Below is a summary of the most significant changes grouped by theme:

### Documentation Updates:
* Removed the `CONTRIBUTING.md` file, with contributing information now linked to an external documentation site in the `README.md`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eca12c0a30e25b4b46522ebf89465a03ba72a03f540796c979137931d8f92055L1-L123) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L98-R98)
* Updated image paths in `README.md` and `docs/mkdocs.yml` to reflect the new directory structure for assets. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L2-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7618337a88ea47f9b778a21f0e17d43eab2aba4880c6be2d95a7bf95e4b8b2dfL10-R22)
* Added `extra.css` stylesheet for custom header logo styling in the documentation.
* Expanded the navigation structure in `docs/mkdocs.yml` to include a new "version" command reference.
* Added a new `rocketship_version.md` file documenting the `version` command.

### CLI Enhancements:
* Introduced a new `version` command to the Rocketship CLI, which prints the version number. This includes the addition of `internal/cli/version.go` and updates to `root.go` to register the command. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7f3fc68830e2dbe627f9d6ba2853977fd7d72edab8bf0c74b2671ec43460b79bR1-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aa84670cfbda5699ea29a1dad10df2df47f189c2748c57f6ea3efff057313658R23)
* Updated `internal/embedded/binaries.go` to make the `DefaultVersion` constant public and used it in the `version` command implementation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fc06b72377ce959db40e16d25dc0c048f0c03e48daff3703c9e109414463f388L16-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fc06b72377ce959db40e16d25dc0c048f0c03e48daff3703c9e109414463f388L73-R73)

### Command Syntax and Usability:
* Standardized the version command syntax in the documentation by replacing `rocketship --version` with `rocketship version`.
* Simplified shell alias examples in `docs/src/installation.md` by removing redundant options.

Fixes #8374

#### Short description of what this resolves:
Enhances the patient context box by displaying the patient's photo alongside their information, improving visual identification of patients throughout the system.

#### Changes proposed in this pull request:
- Adds a new JavaScript file (`patient_context_image.js`) that fetches and displays patient photos in the context box
- Adds CSS styles to properly display and format the patient image
- Modifies the demographics.php file to include the new script

#### Does your code include anything generated by an AI Engine? Yes / No
No

## Installation Instructions
1. Add the JavaScript file:
   - Save `patient_context_image.js` to `interface/main/patient_context_image.js`

2. Add the CSS styles:
   - Add the CSS styles to `interface/themes/style_light.css`
   - Rebuild theme files using one of these methods:
     - For Docker installations:
       ```
       docker exec -i $(docker ps | grep _openemr | cut -f 1 -d " ") sh -c '/root/devtools build-themes'
       ```
     - For non-Docker installations:
       Navigate to the OpenEMR root directory and run:
       ```
       cd interface/themes
       ./build_themes.sh
       ```
       Or check documentation for your specific installation method.

3. Include the script in relevant PHP files:
   - For testing, you can add it to a specific page like `interface/patient_file/summary/demographics.php`
   - For full integration, consider including it in a common header file or template

4. Test with patients with and without photos to verify functionality

## Integration Points
This enhancement interacts with the following OpenEMR components:
- Patient Document API
- UI theme system
- Patient context container

## Browser Compatibility
Tested and working in:
- Chrome 113+
- Firefox 113+
- Safari 16.4+
- Edge 113+
- Mobile browsers (iOS Safari, Chrome for Android)

author: jerseycheese
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description
Refactored the GameSession component from 445 lines to 230 lines by splitting it into smaller, focused components following the Container/Presenter pattern. This improves code maintainability and follows the project's file size constraints (<300 lines per file).

## Related Issue
Closes #361

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Refactoring (code improvements without changing functionality)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test addition or improvement

## TDD Compliance
- [x] Tests written before implementation
- [x] All new code is tested
- [x] All tests pass locally (39 tests, all passing)
- [x] Test coverage maintained or improved

## User Stories Addressed
This PR addresses the technical debt requirement to refactor the GameSession component to meet file size constraints.

## Component Development
- [x] Storybook stories created/updated
- [x] Components developed in isolation first
- [x] Visual consistency verified

## Implementation Notes
Created the following focused components:
- **PlayerChoices**: Handles player choice selection UI with radio button semantics
- **SessionControls**: Manages pause/resume/end buttons with proper ARIA attributes
- **GameSessionLoading**: Displays loading state with customizable message
- **GameSessionError**: Shows error state using existing ErrorMessage component
- **GameSessionActive**: Renders active game session combining all sub-components
- **useGameSessionState**: Custom hook encapsulating all state management logic

All existing behavior has been preserved, including:
- Accessibility features (focus management, screen reader announcements)
- Error handling with retry functionality
- Session state management (pause/resume/end)

This pull request introduces several updates, including the addition of a new GitHub Actions workflow for Canary releases, renaming and updating the release workflow, and dependency updates across multiple files. Below is a breakdown of the key changes:

### GitHub Actions Workflows

* **New Canary Release Workflow**: Added a new workflow (`.github/workflows/canary.yml`) triggered by specific issue comments (`canary-publish` or `/canary-publish`) to automate Canary releases. It includes steps for checking out the PR branch, setting up Node.js and pnpm, and publishing the Canary version using a specified script.
* **Renamed and Updated Release Workflow**: Renamed `.github/workflows/changeset-publish.yml` to `.github/workflows/release.yml` and updated its configuration. Changes include renaming the job from `publish` to `release`, improving step names for clarity, and updating the `changeset-actions/publish` configuration with corrected parameters and formatting. # User Management Module Implementation

This PR implements a complete user management module with the following features:

## New Components
- **Users Page**: Added a dashboard page to view, search and filter users with pagination
- **User Detail Page**: View detailed user information
- **User Form**: Create and edit user functionality with form validation

## Technical Details
- Added reusable `PaginatedTable` component for consistent data tables with pagination
- Implemented form validation using React Hook Form and Zod
- Created user-specific hooks for data management:
  - `useCreateUser`
  - `useUpdateUser`
- Updated routing configuration to support new user management paths

author: stuartp44
body:
This pull request introduces enhancements to the AWS Lambda functions for scaling GitHub Actions runners. Key changes include the addition of functionality to manage runner tags (tagging and untagging). 

- For JIT-instances the GitHub runner id is is added in the tag `ghr:github_runner_id` during registrartion in the scale-up lambda
- For non-JIT-instances the tag `ghr:github_runner_id` is added in in the start script.
- The IAM permission for the runner instances now allows to create only for the instance self to create the tag `ghr:github_runner_id`. 
- The scale down function is using the runner id to efficient check the status of a runner.
- Orphan tags are removed when a runner seems to be active (again).

fix: #4391


### Functionality Enhancements:
* **Tag Management:**
  - Added `untag` function to remove tags from EC2 instances. (`lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/aws/runners.ts`, [lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/aws/runners.tsR117-R122](diffhunk://#diff-69076cf041b0bcf70b90ba1dde121bfc3cb3b57bc9d293d29f7da72affcf0041R117-R122))
  - Updated orphan runner handling to include untagging logic when a runner is no longer orphaned. (`lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.ts`, [lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.tsL197-R261](diffhunk://#diff-2bc035e9625a802da709edd04410265c80ad992a4ead3d76024bcdb001f34d2eL197-R261))

* **JIT Runner Support:**
  - Introduced logic to handle JIT runners by checking their status and activity before untagging or terminating. (`lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.ts`, [lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.tsL197-R261](diffhunk://#diff-2bc035e9625a802da709edd04410265c80ad992a4ead3d76024bcdb001f34d2eL197-R261))
  - Added `runnerId` to runner information for better identification and handling of JIT runners. (`lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/aws/runners.ts`, [lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/aws/runners.tsR95](diffhunk://#diff-69076cf041b0bcf70b90ba1dde121bfc3cb3b57bc9d293d29f7da72affcf0041R95))

### Testing Improvements:
* **Expanded Test Coverage:**
  - Added tests for the new `untag` functionality. (`lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/aws/runners.test.ts`, [lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/aws/runners.test.tsL232-R295](diffhunk://#diff-a41db796ea6eeeb679f8cda3eb91243ffc16e68b8ebbeaea6837fbf85e7241baL232-R295))
  - Enhanced scale-down tests to cover JIT runner scenarios, including untagging and termination logic. (`lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.test.ts`, [lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.test.tsR354-R405](diffhunk://#diff-5ede55c4f52b3aa79e856e42bcd9f5047d38f4ea4edb3903db7bce9fdb65cc38R354-R405))

* **Mock Updates:**
  - Updated mocks to include the new `untag` function for testing purposes. (`lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.test.ts`, [lambdas/functions/control-plane/src/scale-runners/scale-down.test.tsR36](diffhunk://#diff-5ede55c4f52b3aa79e856e42bcd9f5047d38f4ea4edb3903db7bce9fdb65cc38R36))

These changes improve the scalability and robustness of the control-plane functions, ensuring better handling of dynamic runner configurations and edge cases.

### What does this PR do
We render environment variables for bootstrapping in a prior step to bootstrapping, filtering out empty strings, e.g. if `datadog_installer_version` is not set (as is default https://github.com/DataDog/ansible-datadog/blob/5a7dea7132a8e51ba75d602efed07492df53f537/defaults/main.yml#L202), do not add `DD_INSTALLER_DEFAULT_PKG_VERSION_DATADOG_INSTALLER` to the bootstrapping command.

#incident-38697: we break `datadog-agent` E2E by always providing `DD_INSTALLER_DEFAULT_PKG_VERSION_DATADOG_INSTALLER` and `DD_INSTALLER_DEFAULT_PKG_VERSION_DATADOG_APM_INJECT`

author: milan-zededa
body:
# Description

<!-- Clear description what this PR does and why it's needed -->

When an application network configuration depends on a network instance (NI) that is either missing or in an error state, zedrouter flags the `AppNetworkStatus` with `AwaitNetworkInstance`. It then waits until the network instance becomes available and is activated without errors before proceeding with the activation of the application network.

However, conditions may change while the application is waiting for the network instance to be available. For instance, another application with conflicting port forwarding rules could have been deployed during this time, which would necessitate preventing the activation of this app's network.

To address this, we adopt the approach used in `zedrouter.retryFailedAppNetworks()`, where the entire pubsub handler is re-executed to repeat the full validation process. The handler is idempotent, ensuring operations like AppNum allocation reuse previously set values.

(cherry picked from commit e32819eca0caf1062f438ba43b551bf51adf6558)
Backport of PR https://github.com/lf-edge/eve/pull/4458

<!-- For Backport PRs, please note the following:

- Add a note to indicate the origin of the fix, for example:

Backport of #<original-PR-number>

- PR's title should also indicate the stable branch, for instance:

[<stable-branch>] Original's PR title
-->

## PR dependencies

<!-- List all dependencies of this PR (when applicable) -->

## How to test and validate this PR

<!-- Please describe how the changes in this PR can be validated or
verified. For example:

- If your PR fixes a bug, outline the steps to confirm the issue is resolved.
- If your PR introduces a new feature, explain how to test and validate it.
-->

1. Configure a network instance (NI) with an invalid field—EVE will reject the deployment and mark it with an error.
2. Deploy an application connected to this invalid NI—EVE will not deploy the app and will wait for the NI to be fixed.
3. Deploy a second application with identical port forwarding rules as the first one, but connected to a different, valid NI—EVE will successfully deploy this app.
4. Fix the configuration of the previously invalid NI—EVE **should still not deploy** the first application due to port forwarding conflicts with the already deployed second app.

Re-execute full validation for application network config once pending network instances are ready

author: mariyappansubramaniyan
body:
## Problem Statement

We needed to implement a Bitcoin transaction activity screen based on the provided Figma design. The goal was to create a clean, reusable, and scalable component structure that:

* Displays a list of recent Bitcoin transactions
* Shows details like date, status, sender, BTC and fiat value
* Follows Atomic Design principles
* Uses TypeScript and MUI for consistency and type safety

---

## Solution

This PR introduces a fully atomic component-based implementation of the transaction activity screen:

### Atomic Structure

* **Atoms**

  * `Avatar`: shows transaction status icon (success, failed,processing)
  * `Chip`: displays "Purchased" tag
  * `InputField`: used for search
  * `Typography`: standardized text styles

* **Molecules**

  * `DateWithAvatar`: combines date and status icon
  * `TextWithChip`: combines title, subtitle, and chip
  * `AmountWithFiat`: shows BTC and USD amounts
  * `SearchField`: reusable input field with search icon

* **Organisms**

  * `TransactionTable`: renders the scrollable transaction list UI and search field to filter.

### Utilities

* `utils/constants.ts`: centralizes static values (e.g., dummy transaction data)
* `utils/interface.ts`: defines TypeScript interfaces.

### Theming

* `theme/theme.ts`: defines and design theme for consistent UI

### Assets

* `assets/Icons`: contains icons for success/failure /processing status

<!---

Remember that often this will be the only record of our decisions / design, and
our only form of communication with other team members about our changes. So
it's good to be thorough.
-->

# Background / Context
During the installation step of IBI, after setting up the new stateroot we precache the seed cluster's container images. Although there is [support for mirror registries](https://github.com/openshift/installer/blob/main/pkg/asset/imagebased/image/registriesconf.go) when creating the installation ISO, we currently don't account for the seed image containing pull-specs from mirror registries (e.g. the seed image was generated in a cluster with an OCP release image from a private registry). This results in the IBI preparation/installation step to fail when trying to pull images from the mirror registries of the seed cluster, instead of the target cluster's release mirror registries (or the original release registries if no mirror registries are configured on the target cluster).

<!---
Not all reviewers know everything there is to know about the project, use this
section to give a bit of background knowledge about the part of the project
you're changing. Things like links to previous relevant commits, existing
system behavior, how things currently work. Don't describe your changes or what
issue you're solving, just things that are already established. Even if these
seem obvious and the reviewer likely already knows them, it still helps
establish the context of the change.
-->

# Issue / Requirement / Reason for change
We want to support different mirror registry configuration between the seed and the target cluster, in order to enable IBI with seed images generated from disconnected SNO clusters. 

<!---
The reason for making this PR. Use this section to describe the issue you're
solving. The shortcomings of the above background. This doesn't have to be an
actual issue/bug, but could also be a requirement that is being addressed or
the need for a new feature. Don't describe your solution just yet, focus on the
problem/requirement. If there's a relevant ticket, also link it here.
-->

# Solution / Feature Overview

During the IBI preparation step before precaching the seed cluster's images, we can replace the seed release mirror registry with the target release (mirror) registry. That's exactly what we do in IBU [here](https://github.com/openshift-kni/lifecycle-agent/blob/main/controllers/prep_handlers.go#L377-L398).

<!---
Use this section to give a general overview of the solution you're proposing.
Explain how it helps to solve the issue you described above. No need to go into
code specifics.
-->

# Implementation Details

In order to replace the seed release mirror registry with the target release (mirror) registry, we need the seed's release registry and the target's release registry. We can read the first one from the `manifest.json` that's included in the seed image.We can read the second one from the new IBI preparation configuration field `ReleaseRegistry`, which we will add during the creation of the installation ISO.

author: shreyan-gupta
body:
Claping refcounts to 0 was originally introduced in PR https://github.com/near/nearcore/pull/12784/ as a solution to a potential issue with GC of parent shard_uid state when accessed from both children after resharding.

With the new TrieStateResharder as a proper fix where we are replicating the state from parent to both children, we no longer need this fix.

body:
## 🧚 변경사항 설명
1. 필터링 기능 구현을 위한 체크박스 컴포넌트 구현
2. 드롭다운 정렬 기능을 위한 컴포넌트 구현
<!-- 이 PR에서 어떤 변경사항이 있었는지 설명해주세요 -->

## 🧑🏻‍🏫 To-do

<!-- 추가로 작업해야 할 항목이 있으면 체크 박스 리스트로 정리해주세요 -->

## 🎤 공유 사항
### 사용방법
1. **필터링 체크박스(`CheckboxList`)** 사용방법
 - `Checkbox` : 단일 체크박스 컴포넌트 (내부적으로 사용됨)
   - label: 체크박스 옆에 표시될 텍스트
   - count: 선택적으로 표시할 수 있는 개수 (예: "소형이사 (10)")
   - checked: 체크박스 선택 상태
   - onChange: 체크박스 상태 변경 시 호출되는 함수
- `CheckboxList`: **실제 사용할 컴포넌트**
  - title: 체크박스 그룹의 제목
  - items: 체크박스 아이템 배열 (CheckboxItem[])
  - onItemChange: 개별 체크박스 변경 시 호출되는 함수
  - onSelectAll: 전체 선택 버튼 클릭 시 호출되는 함수 
  
2. **드롭다운 정렬 기능(`SortDropdown`)** 사용방법
- 먼저 드롭다운에 표시될 정렬 옵션들을 정의
  - 예 : `const sortOptions = [{ label: "리뷰 많은순", value: "review-desc" }, ...]`
- 컴포넌트 속성 설명
  - options: 위에서 정의한 정렬 옵션 배열을 전달
  - defaultOption: 초기에 선택되어 있을 옵션, 생략하면 첫 번째 옵션이 기본값
  - onChange: 사용자가 새로운 옵션을 선택했을 때 실행될 콜백 함수

<!-- 기타 팀원들이 참고해야 할 사항이 있으면 작성해주세요  -->

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.0.4** to **7.8.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.8.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A number of EncodingWarnings were fixed that could appear if you've enabled
  PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING, fixing `issue 1966`_.  Thanks, `Henry Schreiner
  <pull 1967_>`_.

- Fixed a race condition when using sys.monitoring with free-threading Python,
  closing `issue 1970`_.

.. _issue 1966: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1966
.. _pull 1967: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1967
.. _issue 1970: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1970

.. _changes_7-8-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.8.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- Added a new ``source_dirs`` setting for symmetry with the existing
  ``source_pkgs`` setting. It's preferable to the existing ``source`` setting,
  because you'll get a clear error when directories don't exist. Fixes `issue
  1942`_.  Thanks, `Jeremy Fleischman <pull 1943_>`_.

- Fix: the PYTHONSAFEPATH environment variable new in Python 3.11 is properly
  supported, closing `issue 1696`_.  Thanks, `Philipp A. <pull 1700_>`_.  This
  works properly except for a detail when using the ``coverage`` command on
  Windows.  There you can use ``python -m coverage`` instead if you need exact
  emulation.

.. _issue 1696: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1696
.. _pull 1700: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1700
.. _issue 1942: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1942
.. _pull 1943: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1943

.. _changes_7-7-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.1
   ```
   --------------------------

- A few small tweaks to the sys.monitoring support for Python 3.14.  Please
  test!


.. _changes_7-7-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.7.0
   ```
   --------------------------

- The Coverage object has a new method, :meth:`.Coverage.branch_stats` for
  getting simple branch information for a module.  Closes `issue 1888`_.

- The :class:`Coverage constructor<.Coverage>` now has a ``plugins`` parameter
  for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to `Alex Gaynor <pull
  1919_>`_.

- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized
  away.  For example, previously ``if 13:`` would have been considered a branch
  with one path not taken.  Now it is understood as always true and no coverage
  is missing.

- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you
  are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer.  This should reduce the overhead
  coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable
  ``COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon`` to try it out.

- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

.. _issue 1888: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1888
.. _pull 1919: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1919


.. _changes_7-6-12:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.12
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some aarch64 distributions were missing (`issue 1927`_).  These are now
  building reliably.

.. _issue 1927: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1927

.. _changes_7-6-11:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.11
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed.  The details are in `issue
  1924`_ and `pytest-dev 676`_.  This should reduce the memory footprint for
  everyone even if it hadn't caused a problem before.

- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file.  Thanks, `Russell Keith-Magee
  <pull 1914_>`_.

.. _pull 1914: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1914
.. _issue 1924: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1924
.. _pytest-dev 676: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676

.. _changes_7-6-10:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.10
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were
  incorrect when multi-line statements were involved (`issue 1874`_ and `issue
  1875`_).  These are now fixed.

- Fix: Python 3.14 `defers evaluation of annotations <pep649_>`_ by moving them
  into separate code objects.  That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py
  would mark them as missing, as reported in `issue 1908`_.  Now they are
  ignored by coverage automatically.

- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving
  mocks, imports, and trace functions: `issue 1902`_.  To be honest, I don't
  understand the problem or the solution, but ``git bisect`` helped find it,
  and now it's fixed.

- Docs: re-wrote the :ref:`subprocess` page to put multiprocessing first and to
  highlight the correct use of :class:`multiprocessing.Pool
  <python:multiprocessing.pool.Pool>`.

.. _issue 1874: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1874
.. _issue 1875: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1875
.. _issue 1902: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1902
.. _issue 1908: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1908
.. _pep649: https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#whatsnew314-pep649


.. _changes_7-6-9:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.9
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: `Tomas Uribe fixed <pull 1901_>`_ a performance problem in the XML
  report.  Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

.. _pull 1901: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/1901


.. _changes_7-6-8:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.8
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches
  meant that the entire line was unexecuted.  This isn't true in a few cases:
  the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away.
  Fixes `issue 1896`_.

- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to
  none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception.
  Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, "line 4 didn't jump to
  line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn't jump to line 7 because
  line 4 was always true."  This was also shown in `issue 1896`_.

.. _issue 1896: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1896


.. _changes_7-6-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.7
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild,
  so it's been restored to a conditional.  Sorry for the churn.


.. _changes_7-6-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.6
   ```
   --------------------------

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as
  reported in `issue 1891`_.  The assert has been removed.

.. _issue 1891: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1891


.. _changes_7-6-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.5
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from ``with``
  statements changed how they traced.  This affected whether people saw the
  fix for `issue 1880`_.

- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases
  can cause `bizarre behavior <pytest-cov-666_>`_.

- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to
  asserts.  If you encounter any of these, please let me know!

.. _pytest-cov-666: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/666


.. _changes_7-6-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.4
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: multi-line ``with`` statements could cause contained branches to be
  incorrectly marked as missing (`issue 1880`_).  This is now fixed.

.. _issue 1880: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1880


.. _changes_7-6-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.6.3
   ```
   --------------------------

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing
  branch on the last context manager, as described in `issue 1876`_.  This is
  now fixed.

- Fix: the missing branch message about not exi

author: philippotto
body:
From changelog:
> When you are viewing an annotation and another user changes that annotation, these changes will be automatically shown. For some changes (e.g., when adding a new annotation layer), you will still need to reload the page, but most of the time WEBKNOSSOS will update the annotation automatically.

Implementation details:
- I extended the save saga so that it not only polls for the newest version, but also does try to incorporate newer version from the server, if they exist. I named this incorporation "update action application"
- The update action application does not support all update actions yet (I skipped the ones that I deemed unimportant for this iteration). If an update action cannot be applied, the user is asked to reload the page (as before).
- I refactored the tests and fixtures quite a bit to get the new tests up and running.

Limitations:
- adding/removing layers will still require a reload
- changes to the active mapping will still require a reload <-- this also impacts the very first brush as this will make the null-mapping locked
- meshes aren't refreshed automatically

### URL of deployed dev instance (used for testing):
- https://___.webknossos.xyz

### Steps to test:
- open wk in two different windows (one incognito) and login as sample and sample2
- create a new annotation as sample user and copy a sharing link
- open the same annotation as sample2 (should be read only)
- perform actions as sample and check that all changes are also shown for sample2
- support actions include
  - skeleton related actions
  - volume brushing as well as changing the segment list
  - proofreading operations

## Summary by Sourcery

Refactor and enhance the Transifex file upload process by using async/await, improving logging and error handling (including HTTP 409 handling), and adding upload summary statistics.

Enhancements:
- Refactor uploadTranslatedFileToTransifex to async/await and return a boolean indicating success
- Add detailed logging of file size, upload start/response status, and parseable response data
- Handle HTTP 409 conflict as a successful upload when content already exists
- Parse API error responses for detailed error messages and catch network and parse exceptions
- Track and display total, success, and failure counts for all Transifex uploads in the main script

author: kache
body:
`HedySelect` added an extra round of rendering by using [`innerText`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/innerText), so use `innerHTML` instead, trusting the raw HTML from the server

The raw HTML is already escaped for rendering (evident /w javascript disabled) because the template system escapes by default for safety

Points from contributors meeting:

 * Removing the extra rendering is safe, but loses the "feature" of user-styled `HedySelect` options. This behavior can be safely reintroduced in the future by supporting markdown instead
 * Preemptively HTML escaping user input before db storage is too presumptive. User input could feasibly be used in other places like URLs or SQL queries, so relevant escaping at usage makes more sense.
 * It can still improve usability to allow/block certain characters in user input, but that can be done separately

Testing: [repro video](https://github.com/hedyorg/hedy/issues/6276#issue-2995857046)

Issue: #6276

## Description
This pull request adds expiry date sorting functionality to the URL API, allowing users to organize their URLs based on expiration dates in both ascending and descending order, with special handling for URLs that never expire (NULL values).

## Key Changes
- Added `expiry_date` as a valid sorting option in URL model with NULLS FIRST/LAST handling
- Updated application-level sorting logic in controllers to handle expiry_date sorting
- Added expiry_date sorting in the getUrlsWithStatusFilter function in URL service
- Updated validators to include expiry_date as a valid sortBy value
- Updated API documentation to reflect the new sorting option
- Created memory.md to document implementation details and technical decisions

## Rationale for Changes
This feature enhances user experience by allowing them to easily identify which URLs are expiring soon and prioritize their URL management tasks accordingly. The special handling for NULL values (URLs that never expire) ensures a consistent and intuitive user experience regardless of sorting direction.

## Type of Changes
- [x] New Feature: Adds a new feature to the project
- [x] Documentation: Adds or updates documentation
- [ ] Bug fix: Fixes a bug
- [ ] Refactoring: Code improvement without changing functionality

## Known Issues and Future Improvements
- Performance Optimization: While the current implementation works well for typical user loads, further optimization could be done for extremely large URL collections by implementing database indexing on the expiry_date column.

- UI Integration: The backend API now supports expiry date sorting, but the frontend UI components may need updates to expose this functionality to users through sorting dropdowns or other interface elements.

- Advanced Filtering: In the future, we could extend this feature to include more advanced filtering options, such as combining expiry date sorting with other filters or implementing date range filtering for expiry dates.

author: jemmaldaniel
body:
This PR changes the calibrator model from a logistic regression classifier to an MLP classifier with tuned hyperparameters.

The model architecture comparison script and the hyperparameter tuning scripts can be found on the feat-change-calibrator branch, and the results are on the project GCS bucket. To summarise, I compared the default versions of the following classifier architectures:

- `GradientBoostingClassifier`,
- `HistGradientBoostingClassifier`,
- `XGBClassifier`,
- `RandomForestClassifier`,
- `ExtraTreesClassifier`,
- `SVC`,
- `LogisticRegression`,
- `KNeighborsClassifier`,
- `MLPClassifier`,

training and validating on the combined validation datasets. I used validation AUC, Brier score and calibration error to choose the best classifier architecture. Decision trees and the MLP architecture performed best, and an MLP offers better performance scaling with additional features.

I then found the optimal hyperparameter combination by searching over the grid:

```
param_grid: Dict[str, List[Any]] = {
        "hidden_layer_sizes": [(50,), (100,), (50, 50), (100, 50), (100, 100)],
        "alpha": [1e-5, 1e-4, 1e-3],  # L2 penalty
        "learning_rate_init": [0.001, 0.01, 0.1],
        "max_iter": [200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000],
    }
```

using the same metrics and dataset splits. This gave:
- hidden_layer_sizes=(50, 50)
- learning_rate_init=0.001
- alpha=0.0001
- max_iter=1000

## Overview

This PR improves the wine table filtering by moving the filtering logic from in-memory operations to database-level queries using Dexie.js. This change should improve performance, especially with larger datasets, as filtering happens at the database level rather than on the client side.

## Changes

1. Added new helper functions to `dexie-db.ts`:
   - `getDistinctVintners()` - Retrieves all unique vintner values from the database
   - `getDistinctColors()` - Retrieves all unique color values from the database

2. Updated `WineTable.vue`:
   - Replaced client-side computed `filteredWines` with direct database queries
   - Used Dexie's `where()` and `equals()` for efficient filtering
   - Implemented reactive query updates with `watchEffect`
   - Modified how filter options are populated to always have complete lists

3. Updated tests in `WineTable.spec.ts`:
   - Refactored tests to verify database-level filtering
   - Maintained coverage for all edge cases
   - Ensured all existing functionality works with the new implementation

## Benefits

- **Performance**: Filtering at the database level is more efficient than in-memory filtering
- **Scalability**: Will perform better as the dataset grows larger
- **Maintainability**: Better separation of concerns between data and UI layers

## Testing

All tests are passing, including specific tests for:
- Filtering by vintner
- Filtering by color
- Applying multiple filters simultaneously
- Clearing filters
- Edge cases with empty results

body:
Integrates the existing NLWeb framework to create a prototype Applicant Tracking System (ATS).

Key features implemented:
- Basic Flask web application (`ats_app.py`) for ATS frontend interactions.
- Configuration of Qdrant as the vector database for ATS data.
- Defined new item types (`JobPosting`, `Person`) and tailored prompts in `site_type.xml` for ATS-specific queries.
- Data loading scripts (`ats_data_loader.py`) to ingest job postings and candidate profiles into Qdrant, under "ats_jobs" and "ats_candidates" sites respectively.
- ATS backend calls NLWeb's /ask API to find candidates based on natural language queries, utilizing the RAG capabilities of NLWeb.
- Basic HTML templates for creating jobs, submitting resumes, and searching for candidates.

The prototype demonstrates the feasibility of using NLWeb's core engine for specialized applications like an ATS. I conducted testing via code review and simulated execution due to limitations in running multiple server processes within the automated testing environment.

body:
Description
---
Changed "mod error;" in lib.rs to "pub mod error;" to add support for other projects to handle error cases. Also added a simple comment "Step 1:" to go with the pre-existing "Step 2:" comment for consistency.

Motivation and Context
---
In my project, "cargypto_cli", I needed to do a match case with Seed::generate(). I needed to handle an error case, but noticed that the error::Error enum was private, so I couldn't return the error in a way that satisfies the functional needs of my program. By making  the Error enum public, I was able to handle error cases in my project, as seemingly, some instances of "Seed::generate().unwrap()" fail due to a TryFromInt error. The changes in this pull request should mitigate this issue.

How Has This Been Tested?
---
In the "cargypto_cli" project on my GitHub profile, I was able to successfully handle Error cases by making the Error enum public.

What process can a PR reviewer use to test or verify this change?
---
You could try cloning my repository, "cargypto_cli" and uncomment the original monero_address_creator dependency, and comment out my own dependency I copied into the "libraries" folder, then try executing Seed::generate(), but with .unwrap() added to it. Bulk generation causes some instances of the seed generation to spit out errors, cancelling the wallet generation process. If a user wanted to generate 1000 wallets, they might only end up with, for example, 250, 380, 70, etc... due to Seed::generate().unwrap() failing.

body:
Adds a `sysmon` package that parses Sysmon XML events and maps them to OCSF via UDO-based operators and a comprehensive test suite.

### Review

- The `sysmon-ocsf` stub package (pipelines approach) is superseded by the new `sysmon` package (operator approach) — the stub is intentionally left for now but can be removed in a follow-up.
- EID 1 (Process Create) → OCSF Process Activity (class 1007) is fully mapped; all other EIDs fall back to OCSF Base Event with remaining fields in `unmapped`.
- Test fixtures for all 29 Sysmon event types ship with the package for future coverage expansion.

<details>
<summary>⁉️ Motivation</summary>

Sysmon is one of the most widely deployed Windows endpoint telemetry sources. Having a first-class Tenzir package lets users normalize Sysmon XML events to OCSF in a single operator call, enabling correlation with other OCSF-normalized sources.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🧪 Testing</summary>

- `sysmon/tests/ocsf/01-ProcessCreate.tql` exercises the full EID 1 → OCSF mapping with a real Sysmon XML fixture and golden output.
- Run with `tenzir-test` against the `sysmon` package directory.

</details>

<details>
<summary>📌 References</summary>

- Sysmon documentation: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon
- OCSF Process Activity class: https://schema.ocsf.io/1.7.0/classes/process_activity

</details>

This change passes the user-defined mode all the way down.

body:
RobertK at SD reports this agent string at Schedules Direct

`xmltv.exe (MSWin32) xmltv.exe/1.138 xmltv/1.4.0_003 perl/5.32.1 libwww-perl/6.52`

Looking at the code, I see this
`my $SCRIPT_NAME                = basename("$0"); `

I recommend adding  to 
`$SCRIPT_NAME                = "xmltv.exe::tv_grab_zz_sdjson_sqlite" if $SCRIPT_NAME eq 'xmltv.exe';`

Also, the agent string seems to include the grabber name twice... 
`my $SD = SchedulesDirect->new(UserAgent => "$SCRIPT_NAME ($^O) $SCRIPT_NAME/$SCRIPT_VERSION xmltv/$XMLTV::VERSION`

Unless there is a reason, I reccomend
`my $SD = SchedulesDirect->new(UserAgent => "$SCRIPT_NAME/$SCRIPT_VERSION ($^O)  xmltv/$XMLTV::VERSION`

author: peterager
body:
### Description of change

In #34 code was added to adjust local timestamps to time zone aware timestamps. As it turns out different model Kohler controllers encode this data differently. 

Specifically in rdc2 controllers, the next exercise time is encoded as:

```
    "nextStartTimestamp": "2025-05-26T14:00:00Z"
```

Whereas in the rdc2v4 controllers, the next exercise time is encoded:

```
    "nextStartTimestamp": "2025-04-19T10:00:00",
```

The first one is Zulu / UTC time; the second one is a local time that is missing the timezone context. The code has been updated to handle these cases.

### Visit [app.shiftleft.io] to see the security findings for this repository.

- Forked this demo application
- Generated a unique secret `SHIFTLEFT_ACCESS_TOKEN` to allow GitHub Actions in this repository to communicate with the Qwiet (Shiftleft) API
- Committed a [GitHub Action] that will invoke Qwiet preZero's Static Application Security Testing (SAST) on all future pull requests on this repository
- Created this pull request that demonstrates build rules. It also adds a status check that displays the result of the GitHub Action

Refactor the `update-nord` make goal to add the `NORD_LABEL` with sed since the ROBOT merge does not work. Also, report cases where the synonym looses an existing synonymtypedef since only one is allowed per synonym in the OBO spec.

body:
This PR adds explicit return types to functions in public methods throughout the codebase. The focus was on minimally modifying files to ensure type safety without changing any functionality.

## Changes made:

### In `src/foundation/misc/MiscUtil.ts`:
- Added return type `T` to `valueWithCompensation` 
- Added return type `ArrayBuffer` to `concatArrayBuffers2`
- Added return type `string` to `addLineNumberToCode`
- Added proper return types to utility functions like `isMobileVr`, `isMobile`, `isSafari`, etc.

### In `src/foundation/enhanced_js_objects/Array.ts`:
- Added return type `void` to `enhanceArray`
- Added return type `void` to `enhanceInner`

### In `src/foundation/math/MathUtil.ts`:
- Added return type to `toHalfFloat` function
- Fixed missing return types for various functions like `radianToDegree`, `degreeToRadian`, etc.
- Added explicit types to helper functions like `erf`, `invErf`, `financial`, and others

### In `src/foundation/helpers/MaterialHelper.ts`:
- Added return type `Material` to material creation functions:
  - `createFXAA3QualityMaterial`
  - `createFurnaceTestMaterial`
  - `createGaussianBlurMaterial`
  - `createGammaCorrectionMaterial`
  - `createToneMappingMaterial`
  - `createSummedAreaTableMaterial`
  - `createPanoramaToCubeMaterial`
  - `createPrefilterIBLMaterial`
  - `createEntityUIDOutputMaterial`

All changes are minimal and non-invasive, focusing only on adding explicit return types without modifying any behaviors.

Fixes #1.

author: wozniak
body: Myself and I believe one other person have had issues with a mysterious "failed to load RoninSDK.dll" which I have found to be a result of the logs trying to be created in the Titanfall2 folder, which is owned by admin so regular users can't write to it. This PR moves the logs to the %APPDATA% folder, which doesn't require admin perms to write to.

author: neimasilk
body:
I've implemented the functionality to handle Indonesian words formed by affixing common Indonesian affixes to loanwords.

Key changes:
- I added an `_handle_loanword_affixation` method to `ModernKataKupas` in `src/modern_kata_kupas/separator.py`. This method attempts to identify and segment prefixes and/or suffixes from a word if its base is found in a predefined list of loanwords.
- I integrated this logic into the main `segment` method to be triggered for words not found in the primary root word dictionary.
- I added comprehensive unit tests in `tests/test_separator.py` under a new class `TestLoanwordAffixation`. These tests cover various scenarios, including:
    - Loanwords with prefixes only (e.g., `di-download`).
    - Loanwords with suffixes/clitics only (e.g., `update-an`, `scan-nya`).
    - Loanwords with both prefixes and suffixes/clitics (e.g., `di-scan-nya`).
    - Correct canonical form representation for affixes (e.g., `meN~` for `meng-` or `mem-`).
    - Fallback behavior for unaffixed loanwords and OOV words not matching loanword patterns.
- All 72 tests in the suite pass, ensuring no regressions and validating the new feature.
- I've updated `memory-bank/progress.md` to mark Step 4.1 as complete.

This addresses PRD FR1.7 and aligns with the methodology in Chapter 3.3.5 of the research paper draft.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow (`ci.yml`) that runs tests automatically on pull requests targeting `main` or `develop`.

The pipeline performs the following steps:
- Checks out the repository
- Sets up JDK 21 with Temurin distribution
- Runs `mvn clean verify`, which includes all tests, including Testcontainers integration tests

##Motivation

Ensures code quality by validating that all tests pass before allowing merge, preventing broken code from reaching `main` or `develop`.

## 🧾 Issue

Closes #32

## 🏷️ Branch

`31-ci-workflow-run-tests`

author: erikgaal
body:
This PR adds support of array accessing to the immutable `Psl\Collection` objects.

It does this by hoisting the `ArrayAcess` interface from the `MutableAccessibleCollectionInterface` to the `AccessibleCollectionInterface` contract.

To ensure the immutability of the collections, the immutable versions will still throw an `Error` when setting or unsetting elements via array access.

author: ubparviz
body:
## Added by Parviz

### Added full Uzbek language support to Num2Words

This PR introduces comprehensive support for the Uzbek (uz) language, including:

1. Cardinal numbers — Converts integers and decimals into proper Uzbek words (e.g. 145 -> bir yuz qirq besh).
2. Currency support — Reads over 20 major currencies like USD, EUR, RUB, and UZS in Uzbek (e.g. 123.45 USD -> bir yuz yigirma uch dollar qirq besh sent).
3. Ordinal numbers — Implements to_ordinal method to convert numbers like  "3 -> uchinchi, 21 -> yigirma birinchi".

This significantly improves the localization capabilities of Num2Words and adds value for Uzbek-speaking developers and applications.

Let me know if adjustments or improvements are needed. Thanks!
### Status

- [X] READY
- [ ] HOLD
- [ ] WIP (Work-In-Progress)

### How to verify this change
```Python
from num2words import num2words
print(num2words(42, lang='uz'))  # qirq ikki
print(num2words(5.05, lang='uz', to='currency', currency='UZS'))  # besh soʻm, nol besh tiyin
print(num2words(2025, lang='uz', to='ordinal')) # ikki ming yigirma beshinchi
```

### Additional notes
I decided to add this language because the number of Uzbeks in the world is now approaching 50 million. It clearly reads the numbers you enter in pure Uzbek.

author: martincollignon
body:
## 🛠️ Issue Fix
<!-- Describe the issue this PR fixes -->
fixes #339 
## 💡 Solution
<!-- Briefly describe the solution or changes introduced in this PR -->
- [x] **Added DAGI Bronze Layer**: Fetches Danish administrative data from free DAWA API (https://api.dataforsyningen.dk/) for 4 key layers: municipalities (kommuner), regions (regioner), parts of country (landsdele), and postal codes (postnumre)
- [x] **Added DAGI Silver Layer**: Processes raw GeoJSON into clean, standardized GeoDataFrames with geometry validation, CRS transformation (EPSG:4326 → EPSG:25832), and metadata enrichment
- [x] **CLI Integration**: Added `dagi` as new source option in unified pipeline CLI (`-s dagi`)
- [x] **Automated Workflow**: Integrated into weekly GitHub Actions workflow for automated data updates
- [x] **Dependencies**: Added `aiohttp>=3.10.0` for API requests
- [x] **Error Handling**: Comprehensive retry logic, concurrent processing, and graceful failure handling

**Key decisions:**
- Used free DAWA API instead of token-required WFS service for better accessibility
- Implemented concurrent fetching for all 4 layers to optimize performance
- Added proper geometry validation and CRS standardization for Danish coordinate systems

## ✅ How to Do Self-Test
<!-- Provide instructions for how to test the changes, can be copied from README -->

### Prerequisites
```bash
cd backend/pipelines/unified_pipeline
pip install -e .
```

### Test Bronze Layer (Data Fetching)
```bash
python -m src.unified_pipeline -e local -s dagi -j bronze
```
Expected: Successfully fetches and saves 4 layers (kommuner: 99 features, regioner: 5 features, landsdele: 11 features, postnumre: 1,089 features)

### Test Silver Layer (Data Processing)
```bash
python -m src.unified_pipeline -e local -s dagi -j silver
```
Expected: Processes bronze data into clean GeoDataFrames with proper CRS transformation and no warnings

### Test Complete Pipeline
```bash
python -m src.unified_pipeline -e local -s dagi -j all
```
Expected: Runs both bronze and silver stages sequentially, producing clean administrative boundary data

### Verify CLI Integration
```bash
python -m src.unified_pipeline --help
```
Expected: Shows `dagi` in the source options: `[bnbo|agricultural_fields|cadastral|dagi]`

## 📷 Screenshots (if applicable)
<!-- Add any relevant screenshots for UI changes -->
N/A - This is a backend data pipeline enhancement

## 📝 Additional Notes
<!-- Add any other context or information reviewers should know -->

### Data Coverage
- **Municipalities (kommuner)**: 99 Danish municipalities with full polygon boundaries
- **Regions (regioner)**: 5 Danish regions 
- **Parts of Country (landsdele)**: 11 statistical regions (NUTS3 level)
- **Postal Codes (postnumre)**: 1,089 postal code areas

### Production Impact
- No breaking changes to existing pipeline functionality
- DAGI source runs independently from other sources
- Weekly automated processing scheduled for Sundays at midnight UTC
- All data stored in existing GCS bucket structure (`landbrugsdata-raw-data`)
- Full geometry validation ensures data quality and consistency

### API Source
Using Danish Agency for Data Supply and Infrastructure (DAGI) via their free DAWA API:
- No authentication required
- High reliability and official data source
- Automatically updated by Danish authorities
- Full GeoJSON support with complete geometry data

Check out this video: !v(https://example.com/video.mp4)

author: kaiser0207
body:
The `Player._update_alive_image` method could raise an IndexError when a player (specifically player 2, the "witch") transitioned from moving to idle. This occurred if `self.current_frame`, previously updated based on `self.walk_frames`, was out of bounds for the potentially shorter `self.idle_frames` list.

The fix adds a check within the idle animation logic. If `self.idle_frames` are being used, it verifies if
`self.current_frame` is a valid index for `self.idle_frames`. If not (i.e., `self.current_frame >= len(self.idle_frames)`), `self.current_frame` is reset to 0 before it's used to access the `self.idle_frames` list. This ensures that the index is always valid, preventing the crash.

Lengths of animation lists from animations.py:
- Player 2 (witch) walk_frames: 8
- Player 2 (witch) idle_frames: 6 The error happened when current_frame was >= 6 upon entering idle state.

Arreglo de historia de modificar rol a usuario

## Resumen
Este PR es necesario para arreglar un bug donde el usuario se podía cambiar el rol a si mismo

## ¿Dónde puedo previsualizar esta funcionalidad?
1.  Inicia sesión como usuario "Administrador del Sistema"
2. Entra a la vista de "Usuarios"
3.  Busca el usuario con el que se inició sesión
4. La opción de cambiar el rol debería de estar bloqueada


## Tipos de cambios
- [x] Corrección de error (cambio que soluciona un problema sin afectar otras funcionalidades)
- [ ] Nueva funcionalidad (cambio que agrega una nueva característica sin afectar otras funcionalidades)
- [ ] Cambio disruptivo (corrección o nueva funcionalidad que afecta el funcionamiento esperado)

## Lista de verificación:
- [x] Otro desarrollador ha revisado este PR y lo ha aprobado.
- [x] La rama será eliminada después de la aprobación.

author: rjriajul
body:
## Summary by Sourcery

Add beta support for uploading downloaded videos directly to YouTube by introducing a new `-yt` option, configuration settings, upload flow, and status tracking.

New Features:
- Add `-yt` argument to trigger YouTube uploads in mirror/leech commands
- Introduce YouTube-specific configuration parameters (description, tags, category, privacy) in config files
- Implement YouTubeUpload and YouTubeHelper classes for authenticated video uploads with retry and progress updates
- Integrate YouTube upload flow into the task listener with YtStatus for status reporting

Enhancements:
- Remove deprecated recursive GDrive listing helper
- Add YtStatus class to unify YouTube upload status with existing status utilities
